name: SPT-CL J0304-5404 (Hubble)
blurb: SPT-CL J0304-5404, a massive galaxy cluster acting as a gravitational lens, seen by Hubble.
label: sptdropout0304-hubble
story: Near the core of this galaxy cluster, its gravity appears to magnify a bright, distant galaxy from the Epoch of Reionization into a pair of images. Hubble looked closer to model the lens and to study the galaxy's star-forming clumps.

claims.text: The candidate SPT0304-DO lies in the field of the galaxy cluster SPT-CL J0304-5404, from the South Pole Telescope (SPT) sample
The dropout galaxies appear as multiply imaged pairs near the cores of massive foreground galaxy clusters
The lensed galaxies are exceptionally bright z~7 dropout galaxies in the Epoch of Reionization
The SPT dropouts are very likely young galaxies in the Epoch of Reionization and likely gravitationally lensed and magnified
Hubble's goals: build a strong lensing model and measure resolved star-forming clumps
